name: Necropotence
oracle_text:
Skip your draw step.
Whenever you discard a card, exile that card from your graveyard.
Pay 1 life: Exile the top card of your library face down. Put that card into your hand at the beginning of your next end step.
blocked_sentences: Pay 1 life: Exile the top card of your library face down. Put that card into your hand at the beginning of your next end step.

needs.what: a continuous effect that makes a named player skip a named step -- concretely a `skip_draw_step` entry in `static_effects` (filterless, with the usual `controller`/player spec so it can say "your draw step", "each player's draw step" or "target player skips their next draw step"), backed by a flag the turn walk consults: `turn._draw_step` (src/automtg/engine/turn.py:529-541) must ask the continuous-effects layer before calling `replacements.draw`, and still fire `EventType.DRAW_STEP` afterwards so abilities that watch the step itself keep working. The same hook is what Ob Nixilis, Yawgmoth's Bargain, Solitary Confinement and every "skip your untap step" card would use, so it should take the step name rather than being hard-coded to the draw
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Nothing in the DSL reaches the turn structure. `static_effects` has 34 entries and not one of them touches a step or a phase; `ops` likewise, with the single exception of `skip_untap`, which is not a step effect at all -- `op_skip_untap` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_characteristics.py:259) sets `GameObject.skip_next_untap` (src/automtg/engine/objects.py:298), a per-permanent one-shot cleared by the untap step it skips, so it can say "this creature doesn't untap" and has no vocabulary for "you don't draw". The draw itself has no seam either: `_draw_step` skips only the fixed first-turn rule (`state.turn == 1 and pid == state.starting_player`) and there is no per-player skip flag on the player struct to set; `replacements.draw` (src/automtg/engine/replacements.py:46-66) offers dredge and miracle and has no general replacement hook a static could register against. The `draw_step` trigger event cannot stand in: it is fired at src/automtg/engine/turn.py:541 *after* the draw has already resolved, so a triggered ability hung on it could only clean up afterwards, and the nearest spelling of that -- draw then discard -- is a different card that fires `draw` and `discard` triggers Necropotence's own second line would then feed on.

needs.what: a `delay` whose step is scoped to the *controller's own* turn -- "at the beginning of **your** next end step" as opposed to "at the beginning of the next end step". Concretely a flag on the op (`player: "you"`, or `your_turn_only: true`) recorded on `DelayedTrigger` and honoured in `turn._delay_due` by also requiring `state.active_player == delayed.controller`, alongside the existing step-name comparison
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `op_delay` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_control.py:568-598) records a step name and nothing about whose turn it is, and `_delay_due` (src/automtg/engine/turn.py:188-222) matches on `DELAY_STEPS[step] is state.step` alone. So a delay created by an activation made at instant speed on an opponent's turn -- which is how this ability is used, and the reason the printed line says "your" -- fires at *that opponent's* end step, handing the card over a full turn early and on the wrong side of the opponent's cleanup. `delayed_trigger` with an `end_step` event is no better: its trigger spec has a `controller` clause, but that clause is compared against the event's actor, which for `end_step` is the active player, so it would need the same seat comparison built anyway, and its two durations (`this_turn`, `until_it_fires`, src/automtg/engine/structs.py:784) do not express a turn boundary either. `until_your_next_turn`, which detain and goad already use (ops_combat_flags.py), proves the clock exists in the engine -- it has simply never been wired to `delay`.

needs.what: a way for an ordinary card to exile the top card of its controller's library **face down** and still name that specific card from a later resolution: either a `face_down` flag plus an `as` binding on `look_at_top` (its `_move_found` already special-cases `destination is Zone.EXILE` for the impulse permission, so this is the same seam), or the same pair on `exile` together with a selector that can reach the top of a library. With an `as` binding the return half comes free, because `op_delay` copies `ctx.bindings` at creation (ops_control.py:592) and a delayed `return_to_hand` over `{"binding": "..."}` would then move exactly the one card this activation exiled
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `look_at_top` is the only op that reaches the top of a library, and `_move_found` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_cards.py:309-346) calls `move_object` with no `by` and no face-down marking, and `op_look_at_top` has no `as` binding (the omission ragavan_nimble_pilferer's gap record already names). So the card it exiles is anonymous: it lands in the shared exile zone among everything else ever exiled, no `exiled_by` link is written, and `{"zone": "exile", "exiled_with": "self"}` therefore matches nothing -- a delayed `return_to_hand` written that way would silently hand back no card at all, which is the worst possible failure for a card whose entire function is drawing. `exile` does write `exiled_by` (under `link`) and does take an `as`, but it takes a selector, and `selector_keys` has no way to say "the top card of a library": `{"zone": "library", "count": 1}` is a choice from the whole deck, i.e. a tutor at 1 life. `hideaway` is the one op that gets the exile half nearly right -- with `amount: 1` it exiles the top card face down, sets `exiled_by` and marks it revealed only to its controller (ops_cards.py:1091-1106) -- but it is rule 702.75a's op and not this line: it emits a `hideaway` event, its `amount` means "look at the top N and choose one", and its `_bottom_in_random_order` tail is part of the keyword. Even granting it, the link it leaves is source-wide rather than per-activation, so `exiled_with: "self"` on the delayed return sweeps every card Necropotence still has in exile -- with the mistimed `delay` above, an early-firing return would drag out cards a later activation had not yet paid off.

notes: The middle line, "Whenever you discard a card, exile that card from your graveyard", is NOT blocked and was deliberately not written as a partial answer: `discard` is a trigger event, it is in `OBJECT_SUBJECT_TRIGGERS` (src/automtg/engine/triggers.py:279) precisely so a filter can ask what the discarded card was, and its `_actor` entry makes `controller: "you"` read "you discard" -- so the line is a `discard` trigger whose effect is `exile` over `{"binding": "subject"}`, the card being in the graveyard by the time the event fires.
